clue.text: A simple book

parts.note: a 'simple' is an old word for a medicinal plant, so a book of simples is one describing plants used in remedies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective meaning easy; in old usage it is a noun, a plant used as a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is a book describing plants and their medicinal uses, and such plants were once called simples.

clue.text: English break in to abuse women of household

indicators.note: the letter for English breaks into the word for abuse, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to abuse someone is to do them harm

explanation.surface: An Englishman forces his way in to mistreat the women of a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, and by extension the wives and concubines living there.

clue.text: Herb working to support poor sport

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the herb and the working word follow the poor word

parts.note: poor quality is bad
mint is a common garden herb
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone working with herbs to prop up a poor sporting effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Go miles, travelling to this city

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of the first two words moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to cover many miles to reach a particular city.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Not devious with poker hand?

definitions.meaning: a run of five cards in sequence in poker

explanation.surface: Asking whether an honest player is holding a particular card combination.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest or frank, and in poker it is also a hand of five consecutive cards.

clue.text: Punch contributor who isn't serious

parts.note: reads like a writer for Punch, the British humour magazine, but means someone who throws punches in practice bouts, never fighting for real

explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a long-running British satirical magazine, so the clue suggests a humorous writer; the capital P hides ordinary punching.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's practice opponent trades blows in training without any real contest at stake.

clue.text: Get together to make convenient approximation

definitions.meaning: to gather people or animals into one place
to raise a figure to the next whole number for convenience

explanation.surface: Meeting up to work out a handy estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundup is a gathering of cattle or people, and to round a number upward simplifies it to a convenient figure.

clue.text: Wry expression from serious champion

parts.note: a grim, serious look
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A champion with a serious face pulls a twisted smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a contorted facial expression showing pain, disgust or wry amusement.

clue.text: Not a man who's very desirable?

definitions.text: Not a man who's very desirable?

parts.words: Not a man who's very desirable?
parts.note: seems to describe an unattractive man, but means a woman, not a man, who is alluring and leads others on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man who is undesirable; read it as someone who is not male and who is highly desirable.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who entices others is described by this word, the female form of a tempter.

clue.text: Managed to make millions, by chance

parts.note: to have run a business is to have managed it
to do a dish is to make it
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone ran a business to earn millions, purely through luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random happens haphazardly, without plan, as if by luck.

clue.text: Place to visit where all are tanked up

definitions.text: Place to visit where all are tanked up

parts.words: Place to visit where all are tanked up
parts.note: suggests a bar full of drunks, but means an attraction where the fish all live in tanks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanked up' is slang for drunk; here it means literally kept in tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A public aquarium is a visitor attraction where fish and sea creatures are displayed in water tanks.

clue.text: Seem unable to work a gremlin's at fault

indicators.note: something at fault is out of order, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the article and the word for a mischievous imp, with the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A machine won't run because a gremlin is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at fault' rearranges A GREMLIN; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend illness so as to avoid work.

clue.text: Not cheap, parking inside — time to leave

indicators.note: the parking letter goes inside the word for costly

parts.note: something not cheap is dear
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking in town is expensive, so it is time to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts P within DEAR, giving DEPAR, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away, set off.

clue.text: Role one's given to an irregular

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
one is the Roman numeral I, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A part that an actor takes on is handed to a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a guerrilla fighter, an irregular soldier outside the regular army.

clue.text: Some sentences running consecutively

parts.note: suggests prison terms served one after another, but means sentences of writing following on in a block

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentences running consecutively' is legal language for jail terms served back to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A block of text made up of a group of written sentences on one topic.

clue.text: Strange hope, to be a goddess

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the word hope oddly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd hope of becoming divine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Phoebe is a Titan associated with the moon, and the name is also used for Artemis.

clue.text: Regulation once about rand I exchange

indicators.note: exchange suggests the letters swapping places, as currency changes hands

explanation.surface: A rule about trading South African rands in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges ONCE plus RAND I; the rand is South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative rule or decree, especially a local bylaw.

clue.text: Maybe poured own Scotch-embarrassed about it

indicators.note: the colour of embarrassment goes around the Scots word, enclosing it

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
ain is the Scots form of own

explanation.surface: Someone poured their own whisky and was red-faced about it.
explanation.walkthrough: AIN is Scots for 'own'; 'about' puts RED around it. 'Maybe' marks pouring as one kind of raining.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy rain pours down, so having poured is one example of having fallen from the sky.

clue.text: Preamble to Italian sacred chant

parts.note: an intro is an introduction or preamble

explanation.surface: An opening passage leading into a holy Italian song.
explanation.definitionFit: The introit is the psalm or antiphon sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: A little raised platform inside for artist

indicators.note: the platform word goes inside the turned word for a small amount
in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tad is a little
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A small raised stage put up for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TAD into DAT; 'inside' puts DAIS within it, after DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dadaist belonged to Dada, the early twentieth-century anti-art movement.

clue.text: Worst place to receive praise and clapping

indicators.note: the worst place takes the praise word inside it, receiving it

parts.note: the pits is the worst place imaginable
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Even the worst venue gets praise and applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' is slang for the very worst.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaudits are expressions of approval, such as applause.

clue.text: Criminal laid arm on officer

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their honest order

explanation.surface: A crook lays hands on a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges LAID ARM; the scan's 'am' lost the R.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a top-ranking naval officer commanding a fleet.

clue.text: Extremely upset, having got inside out?

definitions.meaning: with the innards removed, as a fish is cleaned

explanation.surface: Someone distraught after turning out what was inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted is British slang for deeply disappointed, and literally means disembowelled.

clue.text: Men dried, alas — got prompted

indicators.note: alas marks something gone wrong, so the letters of the first two words are disordered

explanation.surface: Men dried off and were reminded of something regrettable.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prompted is to be jogged into remembering something.

clue.text: Filthy from home improvements? That's about right

indicators.note: the home-improvement abbreviation goes about the right abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, covers home improvements

explanation.surface: Home improvement jobs leave you covered in grime, which is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty means grimy, soiled.

clue.text: Notice choice of child care system

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: An advertisement offering a choice of childcare.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the legal process of taking another's child into one's family as one's own.

clue.text: Athlete's agent

definitions.meaning: a messenger or go-between who acts for someone

explanation.surface: A sportsman's representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who races, and also a messenger or agent, as in the old Bow Street Runners of London.

clue.text: Trouble with ingredient for cuppa

definitions.meaning: difficulty, a fix, as in being in for it
what is poured on the teabag to brew a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Problems with making a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuppa' is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hot water is to be in trouble, and boiling water is what brews a pot of tea.

clue.text: General method to get freedom of action

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A general's method for winning room to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is latitude, scope to act as one chooses.
